The factory matrix prints 43 RIGHT FLIPPER LANE CHANGE SWITCH; Figure 4 draws it in a dashed circle beside the upper right flipper. The contact's mounting and construction are unresolved. In PinMAME core_updateSw copies public 82 into 43 every update. Drive 82; direct 43 is overwritten. The single-write button probe proves the emulator copy, not the factory contact's location or polarity. The script's redundant 43 write has no independent effect.

mechanisms.behavior: One ball drains under the apron onto switch 9; output 1 kicks it into the feed path to the shooter lane. The manual plunger launches it. Startup game-on enables play; a held drain contact can cause repeated serve attempts. The table's BallRelease is the final shooter proxy, not an extra physical trough coil. No production multiball trough exists.
mechanisms.label: Single-ball outhole and manual shooter

mechanisms.behavior: Ball enters the spade saucer and holds switch 15; output 2 ejects it to the open field, releasing the contact. P-O-K-E-R/rule lamps control awards, not an additional lock mechanism. A lingering contact can be retried; actual kick strength, trajectory and animation timing are table-owned.
mechanisms.label: Spade Ace saucer

mechanisms.behavior: Ball enters the heart saucer and holds switch 29; output 3 ejects it to the open field, releasing the contact. P-O-K-E-R/rule lamps control awards, not an additional lock mechanism. A lingering contact can be retried; actual kick strength, trajectory and animation timing are table-owned.
mechanisms.label: Heart Ace saucer

mechanisms.behavior: Ball enters the club saucer and holds switch 22; output 15 ejects it to the open field, releasing the contact. P-O-K-E-R/rule lamps control awards, not an additional lock mechanism. A lingering contact can be retried; actual kick strength, trajectory and animation timing are table-owned.
mechanisms.label: Club Ace saucer

mechanisms.behavior: Order 10,J,Q,K,A. Each target slides in guides, latches up and drops with spring bias when struck. Its original horseshoe PCB closes at full down and stays closed until raised. Outputs 4,5,6,7,8 individually raise 10,J,Q,K,A; output 21 operates the common release and drops all five. Out-of-order targets reset individually; held contacts after a reset can cause ROM retries. Original bank photos show five separate plungers and perpendicular release. A generic single-lift bank is incorrect. Guide/contact friction, worn PCB tracks or springs can cause sticking, failed registration or rebound. No numeric mechanical timing is asserted.
mechanisms.label: Five individually reset diamond drop targets and common release

mechanisms.behavior: Scoring contact 35 and its dedicated special-trigger circuit operate the same center jet assembly. Game-on23 gates the response; PinMAME's switch-driven slot publishes 17. Coil movement strikes the ball and returns mechanically. Gameplay confirms the address pair; there is no motor/home-position model.
mechanisms.label: Center Jet

mechanisms.behavior: The left cabinet button operates one flipper, the right operates both right flippers. Hardware EOS switches reduce coil power locally; the CPU only enables their supply. Public 45-48 are synthetic paired states, not individual CPU coil drivers or EOS measurements. Right 82 also supplies ROM lane-change 43. Springs return bats at release; table geometry and tuning remain table-owned.
mechanisms.label: Three cabinet-wired flippers

mechanisms.behavior: A passing ball rotates the free spinner and pulses 17. Royal Flush 3X/spinner lamp 18 changes the award; no motor or actuator is fitted.
mechanisms.label: Left passive spinner
